answer: A proof-of-burn protocol deters Sybil attacks by forcing agents to provably incinerate tokens before gaining market admission. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of destroyed currency per identity, proving registration is not an unsubstantiated fable. Genuine agents recoup this burn through commerce, such as settling deliveries of refined copper or grading sable fibers. However, this sunk cost excludes bootstrap agents and cannot deter well-funded cartels.
